findings.claim: Original 0045EBD0 initializes the class-1 root 16-word transform from 004FAED8, including direction root+0x30..0x38 = (0,0,1). With a controlled class-1 context the selected GTSi and bus full original 004AD6F0 VCF loaders retain these dwords, and native 004572B0 registration also preserves them, creates entry 00542830 and raises root refcount 3 to 4.
findings.limitations: Only Win32 HeapAlloc and other OS/resource services substituted, vehicle-class context bound under harness; original creator CALL not executed uninterrupted and no actual simulation tick.

findings.claim: Original 00406AB0 default camera for selected native-root GTSi and bus executes past the original class-0x28 VLOC attachment guard through 00437F90 and 00472990; original 00437F90 output has zero nonfinite words out of 16 and six double fields at 004C2730+0x160..+0x18F are all finite following native 00405970 projection initialization.
findings.limitations: Original Win32 and resource/palette services substituted; trigonometric and float-to-int mathematical boundaries explicitly substituted; fixed viewport/clock; no hardware x87 or real camera pose parity.

findings.claim: Selected bus built and natively registered through the same VCF, VLOC, active-entry and camera path but with a manually zeroed root has exactly nine nonfinite original 00437F90 float32 output words and six NaN camera double fields; substituting original 0045EBD0 root initialization alone yields zero in both categories.
findings.limitations: Causal inference in a controlled Ghidra-original-instruction harness, not evidence of NaN in the actual retail Windows game. Other root-pose patterns untested.

findings.claim: Hardware x87 numerical parity, physically accurate camera pose, game-frame scheduling, class-1 simulation pose updates, multiple consecutive frames and complete raster output remain unverified despite finite selected-camera fields in this experiment.
findings.limitations: Finite is necessary but insufficient for numerical accuracy or physically valid transform; Ghidra emitted floating-point/uninitialized-read warnings.
